title: H_1 of the naive cotangent complex of a presentation: maps induced by morphisms of presentations (Stacks 00S1, parts (2), (3) on H_1)
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $S$ an $R$-algebra. A *presentation* of $S$ over $R$ is a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\alpha:P\to S$ where $P=R[x_t,\ t\in T]$ is a polynomial ring over $R$ on an arbitrary set $T$ of variables; let $I=\ker\alpha$. Its *naive cotangent complex* is the two-term complex of $S$-modules $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha):\ I/I^2\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm d_\alpha\ }S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$, $f\bmod I^2\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm df$ ($\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; $I/I^2$ is an $S=P/I$-module and $\mathrm d_\alpha$ is well defined and $S$-linear by the Leibniz rule), and $H_1(\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)):=\ker\mathrm d_\alpha$. Now let $R\to R'$ and $\psi:S\to S'$ be ring homomorphisms, where $S'$ is an $R'$-algebra, such that the square commutes ($\psi(r\cdot1_S)=r\cdot1_{S'}$ for $r\in R$, $R$ acting on $S'$ through $R'$); let $\alpha:P\to S$ be a presentation of $S$ over $R$ and $\alpha':P'\to S'$ a presentation of $S'$ over $R'$, with kernels $I$, $I'$. A *morphism of presentations* from $\alpha$ to $\alpha'$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\varphi:P\to P'$ ($P'$ an $R$-algebra through $R\to R'$) with $\alpha'\circ\varphi=\psi\circ\alpha$. For such $\varphi$: $\varphi(I)\subseteq I'$; the map $\varphi_1:I/I^2\to I'/I'^2$, $f\bmod I^2\mapsto\varphi(f)\bmod I'^2$, is $S$-linear ($S$ acting on $I'/I'^2$ through $\psi$), satisfies $\mathrm d_{\alpha'}\circ\varphi_1=\varphi_0\circ\mathrm d_\alpha$ for the $S$-linear map $\varphi_0:S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}\to S'\otimes_{P'}\Omega_{P'/R'}$, $s\otimes\mathrm dg\mapsto\psi(s)\otimes\mathrm d\varphi(g)$, and hence restricts to an $S$-linear map $\varphi_*:H_1(\mathrm{NL}(\alpha))\to H_1(\mathrm{NL}(\alpha'))$. Moreover: (1) if $\varphi,\varphi'$ are two morphisms of presentations from $\alpha$ to $\alpha'$ (over the same square), then $\varphi_*=\varphi'_*$; (2) $\mathrm{id}_P$ is a morphism of presentations from $\alpha$ to itself (over the identity square) and $(\mathrm{id}_P)_*$ is the identity; if $\varphi$ is a morphism of presentations from $\alpha$ to $\alpha'$ and $\varphi'$ one from $\alpha'$ to a presentation $\alpha'':P''\to S''$ of $S''$ over $R''$ (over a second commuting square $R'\to R''$, $\psi':S'\to S''$), then $\varphi'\circ\varphi$ is a morphism of presentations from $\alpha$ to $\alpha''$ over the composite square and $(\varphi'\circ\varphi)_*=\varphi'_*\circ\varphi_*$.
